task: Focused complete-pipeline comparison of Flat Tree, original Linear and Legacy on twelve fresh cases
authorization: User explicitly requested concentrating on Flat Tree, Linear and Legacy; continue the existing user-approved cumulative USD200 task budget without increase or reset.

mode_definitions.flat_tree: Current corrected source-bearing tree plus bounded flat indexed plan and existing-call condition/assertion review; no explicit topology in plan/delivery.
mode_definitions.linear: Original free-text incremental notes; no argument tree, no grounded review.
mode_definitions.legacy: Original incremental argument tree and endpoint battlefield preparation; no correction-enabled state or early rebuttal plan. Uses shared current fixes/defaults, not a checkout of the historical repository.

estimate.basis: 72 fresh generations/judgments, approximately 800 generation calls; allow up to 8M generator input/0.6M output and 72 judgments at <=4K input/1600 output, plus diagnosed bounded failures. No paid compute provisioned.
estimate.uncertainty: Rates/tokens and conservative failure accrual, not an invoice; no additional paid compute/storage provisioned.

budget.guard: Every request reserves full conservative bound atomically before dispatch; successful verified receipts settle at 4x usage, errors/unknown retain bounds. Reject dispatch above cumulative cap. No automatic retry or restart.
budget.stop: Stop only these run workers if accounting fails or cap blocks dispatch; preserve saved answers and artifacts. No new paid compute provisioned.

retry_policy: No regenerated saved answers or replaced judgments. At most one unchanged missing-judge retry after diagnosis; exhausted judgments remain missing. No automatic HTTP retries or worker restart.
primary_comparisons: flat_tree vs linear: case-paired condition coverage
flat_tree vs legacy: case-paired condition coverage
secondary_comparisons: Rebuttal strength, strawman and unsupported-fact flags
Text-ready latency, total generation tokens/cost/calls including setup
Linear vs Legacy; descriptive case-kind and assigned-side groups
Flat valid-plan and raw-prefix fallback counts; inspect delivered answers
missing_data_policy: At most one unchanged missing-judge retry after diagnosis. Exclude an entire case from paired judgment comparisons when either arm lacks a repeat. Retain all generated answers; report generation time/cost on all answers.
limitations: Fresh authored cases, not a standard or representative debate benchmark; twelve independent cases, two model samples each.
Methods differ in correction, planning, grounding and revision as well as tree use; compares complete pipelines, not isolated tree topology.
Flat was selected using previous cases; new case outputs remain untouched during this frozen verification. Do not compare absolute scores directly to earlier case sets.
Six assigned-for and six assigned-against cases; three cases per kind are too few for reliable subgroup rankings.
All arms use exact target matching and no embedding fallback; this may particularly affect legacy relation attachment.
All arms receive identical fixed history/evidence, model, token caps and one feedback/revision pass, but their prompts and number of preparatory calls intentionally differ.
Automatic judging may miss semantic errors or apply composite checks inconsistently; preserve judgments and report spot checks separately.
Text-only simulated endpoint latency excludes ASR/TTS; pricing and usage remain provisional.
offline_preflight: Unchanged inference source previously passed 335 tests +42 subtests; focused policy/history/feedback/budget suite now passes 41 tests. Cases validated for unique IDs/motions, side/history consistency and predefined three-check rubric; report compilation passes.
